counterfactual_missing_items: No bilateral facial weakness or eye abduction deficit is described.
No limb, palate, or tongue anomalies are described.
Symmetric forehead, eye closure, and nasolabial folds directly contradict Moebius syndrome.
decisive_items: When she smiles, the right lower lip deviates inward; frowning, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, and nasolabial fold depth are symmetric on both sides.
the right lower lip deviates inward, whereas the rest of facial movement is symmetric

Magnetic resonance imaging of the temporal bones and internal auditory canals is normal, echocardiography shows no cardiac anomalies, and an auditory brainstem response test reveals normal hearing pathways.
response.rationale: R3 matches isolated congenital unilateral lower lip palsy: isolated right lower lip depression weakness with otherwise symmetric facial movement, normal neurodevelopment, and normal MRI, echocardiography, and hearing. R2 Moebius syndrome requires congenital facial diplegia with impaired eye abduction and often additional anomalies; the symmetric eye closure, forehead wrinkling, nasolabial folds, and normal imaging/echo/ABR directly contradict it.

rejected.why: Moebius syndrome would require bilateral facial weakness and impaired eye abduction; here eye closure, forehead wrinkling, and nasolabial folds are symmetric, and MRI/echo/ABR are normal.
